SMTO-WEB-0018 — An older research record mentions missing research setup

GUID: 8fc64aa6-e73e-5521-9c9c-81b44c1bc21a
Slug: research-contract-missing
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • This message comes from an older saved record. Today's SMTO sets up research automatically when Web Research is used, so it does not prove your current answer was blocked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the latest run in this conversation and check whether an answer appeared. This message is from an older record, so your current request may have finished normally.
  2. If no answer appeared and you wanted web research, select the capabilities button near the message box (it shows Capabilities or Enabled). Make sure Web Research is checked, then select Apply. SMTO only sets up research tracking when the Web Research skill is chosen for the conversation.
  3. If no answer appeared, send your request again in a new message. A new request starts fresh research tracking instead of relying on the old record.

What success looks like

  • A new research request finishes with an answer and no message about missing research setup.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting where you saw the message (which run or screen). Don't treat this message alone as proof that research failed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Retained catalog alias research_contract_missing: a saved diagnostic reports missing research intent, but current code (web_research/runtime.py ensure) builds research state whenever Web Research is selected and has no emitting site for this reason.

What this means

  • This retained alias describes missing research intent, while current ensure builds research state when the skill is selected and proof validation returns without rejecting absent research. This retained catalog alias has no direct current emitting site. The related runtime behavior supplies context only; the alias alone does not establish that the check ran, publication was blocked, or a model call failed.

Why this can happen

  • This retained alias describes missing research intent, while current ensure builds research state when the skill is selected and proof validation returns without rejecting absent research.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the emitting version and whether this run has selected research state.

How to fix it

  • Treat this as a historical diagnostic: identify where it was recorded (run trace, event log or imported state) before acting. If research behavior is actually required, confirm the web_research skill is in the run's selected skill IDs so ensure() freezes research state; do not infer a current missing intent from this alias.
  • Inspect the run's selected research skill and retained intent; use supported task initialization when research state is actually required.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • Current research setup and the original diagnostic source are identified before choosing recovery.

What not to do

  • Do not invent research requirements or claim that this retained diagnostic proves a current missing intent.

Technical notes

  • This retained catalog alias has no direct current emitting site. The related runtime behavior supplies context only; the alias alone does not establish that the check ran, publication was blocked, or a model call failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
